chapter: Decca, Cow Cow Blues and royalties
title: Cow Cow Davenport, Mayo Williams and the road to Decca
summary: Cow Cow Blues opened the doors of Decca and world venues for Price; he recalls Mayo Williams looking for someone to play for the stricken Cow Cow in 1938.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: ...it was over. It was over when he made records. But I was lucky in this way, Dan,, to work with Decca Records. This rarely happened. All because Cow Cow Davenport taught me the "Cow Cow Blues." I probably would have just been around, you know. But no, I had more initiative than just to be around, but I don't know if I would have ever had an opportunity to say that I played the Metropole or to say that I played the Apollo or to say that I played the Olympia in Paris, or that I played at the Salle Playel, or that I played the Drury Lane Theatre in London or, you know what I mean, or that I did a Radio Diffusion, or that I did a Bavarian television show. I doubt if I didn't know the "Cow Cow Blues"...because...you know the story about that, don't you?...Mayo Williams came to town with Cow Cow. Cow Cow had arthritis and he'd had a stroke, a partial stroke. He couldn't

play. This was in 1938 and they were stopping at the Woodside Hotel and I saw Jack, Count Basie's valet... he said that Mayo Williams was in town, looking for somebody to play for Cow Cow Davenport. I didn't say anything to him. I went and I met Mayo. We renewed our acquaintance. He/told me that if I ever come to New York, look him up.
